task_description:
# Layered JSON Settings Resolver on Gel 7.1

## Background

A **Gel 7.1** database runs locally inside this container and already holds a seeded settings
catalog. Each settings *record* owns a chain of *layers*; every layer stores one nested JSON
document (defaults, group overrides, per-user overrides). Your job is to build the command-line
engine that collapses a record's chain into a single effective document and that safely patches
a layer of that chain.

## Environment

- Project path: `/home/user/settings-engine` (it already contains `gel.toml` and `dbschema/`
  with the migration for the schema below already applied).
- The Gel 7.1 server runs inside this container. `/usr/local/bin/gel-start.sh` starts it if it is
  not running, blocks until it is ready, and is safe to run repeatedly.
- Schema, in module `default` on branch `main`:
  - `SettingsLayer` with properties `key: str` (exclusive), `tier: str`, `doc: json`,
    `active: bool`, `revision: int64`.
  - `SettingsRecord` with properties `slug: str` (exclusive), `label: str`, and
    `multi layers: SettingsLayer` carrying the link property `precedence: int64`.
- Guaranteed about the data: every `doc` is a JSON object; every layer link has a `precedence`
  value; the `precedence` values inside one record are distinct; a layer may be shared by
  several records; `precedence` is unrelated to `tier`, to `key` ordering and to insertion order.

## Requirements

Implement a re-runnable CLI whose entrypoint is exactly
`python3 /home/user/settings-engine/settings_engine.py`. It is always invoked with
`/home/user/settings-engine` as the working directory and supports exactly two subcommands.

### `resolve`

```
python3 /home/user/settings-engine/settings_engine.py resolve --slug <slug>
```

Resolves the record identified by `<slug>` and prints the result envelope described below.

### `patch`

```
python3 /home/user/settings-engine/settings_engine.py patch --slug <slug> --layer <layer_key> --file <path>
```

Reads a JSON document from `<path>`, folds it into the stored `doc` of the layer whose `key` is
`<layer_key>` (which must be one of that record's own layers), increases that layer's `revision`
by exactly 1, and then prints the result envelope for `<slug>` computed from the state *after*
the patch. Nothing else in the database may change: no other layer, no other property, no link.

### Resolution rules

The effective document starts as an empty JSON object and is built by folding in the `doc` of
each **active** layer of the record, in ascending `precedence` order. Layers whose `active` is
false are skipped entirely. Folding an override object `O` into an accumulator object `A` is
defined per key `k` of `O`:

1. if `O[k]` is JSON `null`: remove `k` from `A` if it is present; `k` is absent from the result.
2. otherwise, if `O[k]` is a JSON object: let `B` be `A[k]` when `A[k]` exists and is itself a
   JSON object, and the empty object otherwise; `A[k]` becomes the result of folding `O[k]`
   into `B`.
3. otherwise: `A[k]` becomes `O[k]`. Arrays and scalars are never merged or combined
   element-wise; they replace whatever was there.

Consequently the effective document never contains a JSON `null`.

Every removal that rule 1 actually performed (i.e. the key was present) is recorded as a *path*:
the array of key names leading from the root of the document to the removed key. A rule-1 key
that was not present is not recorded. Only the removed key's own path is recorded, never the
paths of its descendants. A recorded removal stays recorded even if a later layer re-creates the
key.

### Patch rules

Folding the patch document `P` into the target layer's stored `doc` uses the same recursive
object merge, with exactly one difference: a JSON `null` in `P` is **stored**. That is, per key
`k` of `P`: `null` sets `doc[k]` to JSON `null`, creating `k` if absent and discarding whatever
value or subtree was there; a JSON object folds recursively into `doc[k]` when `doc[k]` exists
and is an object, and into the empty object otherwise; anything else replaces `doc[k]`.
Keys of the stored document that the patch does not mention keep their previous values.

### Result envelope

Exactly one line on stdout: a JSON object with exactly these five keys.

- `applied_layers`: array of the `key` values of the layers that were folded in, in the order
  they were folded.
- `deleted_paths`: array of the recorded removal paths (each path is an array of strings),
  duplicates removed, sorted lexicographically by segment sequence: compare segments pairwise by
  Unicode code point, and a path that is a proper prefix of another sorts first.
- `document`: the effective document.
- `revision`: the sum of the `revision` values of the layers listed in `applied_layers`.
- `slug`: the resolved record's `slug`.

Serialization is strict: every JSON object in the output — the envelope and every nested object,
at any depth — has its keys ordered ascending by Unicode code point; there is no whitespace
between JSON tokens (in particular no space after `:` or `,`); non-ASCII characters are written
literally as UTF-8 and never as `\uXXXX` escapes; booleans and numbers keep their JSON types; the
line is terminated by a single newline and nothing else is written to stdout.

### Errors and exit codes

- `0`: success.
- `3`: no record with the requested `slug` exists.
- `4`: (`patch` only) the requested layer is not one of that record's layers, including the case
  where no layer with that `key` exists at all.
- `5`: (`patch` only) the patch file cannot be read, does not contain valid JSON, or its
  top-level JSON value is not an object.

If more than one of these applies, the smallest applicable code is used. On every non-zero exit,
stdout must stay empty, a diagnostic must be written to stderr, and the database must be left
completely unchanged.

### Concurrency

Up to 8 `patch` invocations may run simultaneously against the same layer of the same record.
Every one of them must exit `0`, each of them must increase that layer's `revision` by exactly 1
(so the final revision equals the initial revision plus the number of invocations), and no key
written by any of them may be missing or stale in the stored document afterwards.

### Additional constraints

- `resolve` never writes to the database, and two identical invocations produce byte-identical
  stdout.
- Every invocation must reflect the live contents of the database: records, layers, documents,
  `active` flags, `revision` values and chain memberships can be added or changed by other tools
  between two invocations, and the very next invocation must already account for that.
- Do not change the seeded schema, and do not change seeded rows other than through the patch
  behaviour specified above.

  Python client are all installed in the image, no network access, credentials or external
  services are involved.

# Verification Plan

## Setup

1. Run `/usr/local/bin/gel-start.sh` and wait until the local Gel 7.1 server accepts
   connections (the server takes a while to become ready; poll before doing anything else).
   Every step below, including every step that shells out to the `gel` CLI, must depend on that
   readiness.
2. Confirm `/home/user/settings-engine/settings_engine.py` exists.
3. Restore the mutable fixtures to their baseline so that verification is re-runnable, using a
   direct database write:
   - layer `patch.user`: `doc` = `{"a": {"b": 2}}`, `revision` = 0
   - layer `patch.shadow`: `doc` = `{"shadow": true}`, `revision` = 0
   - layer `race.user`: `doc` = `{}`, `revision` = 0
4. Remove any leftovers of the dynamic fixtures from a previous run (record `zz-dynamic` first,
   then layers whose `key` starts with `dyn.`), then create them fresh:
   - layer `dyn.mid`: tier `group`, `doc` = `{"p": {"q": 9}, "only": "mid"}`, active, revision 7
   - layer `dyn.base`: tier `global`, `doc` = `{"p": {"q": 1, "r": 2}, "arr": [1, 2, 3]}`,
     active, revision 4
   - layer `dyn.off`: tier `user`, `doc` = `{"nope": 1}`, **not** active, revision 100
   - layer `dyn.top`: tier `user`, `doc` = `{"p": {"q": 42}}`, **not** active, revision 1
   - record `zz-dynamic`, label `Dynamic`, linked to `dyn.mid` with `precedence` 5, `dyn.base`
     with `precedence` 100, `dyn.off` with `precedence` 7 and `dyn.top` with `precedence` 200
5. Delete any patch input files the checks below create before (re)creating them.

## Seeded fixtures (already in the database)

Layers (`key`, `tier`, `active`, `revision`, `doc`):

- `base.global`, global, active, revision 3:
  `{"theme": "light", "limits": {"cpu": 2, "mem": 512, "nested": {"deep": {"a": 1, "b": 2}}},
  "features": ["a", "b"], "flags": {"beta": false, "gamma": true}, "keep": "global",
  "": "empty-key-global", "1": "one", "2": "two", "10": "ten", "id": "global-id",
  "__type__": "global-type"}`
- `user.alice`, user, active, revision 0:
  `{"theme": "solar", "limits": {"cpu": 8}, "keep": null, "extra": {"x": {"y": {"z": true}}},
  "id": 5}`
- `group.engineering`, group, active, revision 0:
  `{"theme": "dark", "limits": {"mem": 1024, "nested": {"deep": {"b": null, "c": 3}}},
  "features": ["c"], "flags": null, "日本語": "group", "emoji🙂": "group"}`
- `override.disabled`, group, **not** active, revision 41: `{"theme": "MUST-NOT-APPLY",
  "limits": null}`
- `user.bob`, user, active, revision 0:
  `{"limits": {}, "features": {}, "flags": {"beta": {}}, "theme": {"nested": true},
  "": null, "missing": null, "1": null}`
- `base.empty`, global, active, revision 0: `{}`
- `noop.disabled`, user, **not** active, revision 0: `{"a": 1}`
- `ghost.a`, group, **not** active, revision 0: `{"ghost": 1}`
- `ghost.b`, user, **not** active, revision 0: `{"ghost": 2}`
- `patch.base`, global, active, revision 0: `{"a": {"b": 1, "c": [1, 2]}, "z": "zed"}`
- `patch.user`, user, active, revision 0: `{"a": {"b": 2}}`
- `patch.shadow`, group, **not** active, revision 0: `{"shadow": true}`
- `race.base`, global, active, revision 0: `{"seed": "kept", "counterparts": {"pre": 1}}`
- `race.user`, user, active, revision 0: `{}`
- 300 filler triples, for `i` from 0 to 299 with `n` = `i` zero-padded to 4 digits:
  `fill-<n>.g` (global, active, revision 0, `{"g": {"i": <i>}}`),
  `fill-<n>.u` (user, active, revision 0, `{"u": {"i": <i>}, "g": {"x": true}}`),
  `fill-<n>.x` (user, **not** active, revision 0, `{"x": 1}`)

Records (`slug`, `label`, chain as `layer key`@`precedence`):

- `acme-alice`, `Acme / Alice`: `base.global`@10, `user.alice`@50,
  `group.engineering`@200, `override.disabled`@999
- `acme-bob`, `Acme / Bob`: `base.global`@10, `user.bob`@20
- `solo-empty`, `Solo Empty`: `base.empty`@1, `noop.disabled`@2
- `ghost-town`, `Ghost Town`: `ghost.a`@1, `ghost.b`@2
- `orphan-record`, `Orphan`: no layers at all
- `patch-target`, `Patch Target`: `patch.base`@10, `patch.user`@90, `patch.shadow`@95
- `race-target`, `Race Target`: `race.base`@10, `race.user`@20
- 300 filler records `fill-<n>`, label `Filler <n>`, chain `fill-<n>.g`@10, `fill-<n>.u`@20,
  `fill-<n>.x`@30

## Verification Steps

All commands below are run with `/home/user/settings-engine` as the working directory. "Canonical
JSON" means: keys of every object sorted ascending by Unicode code point, no whitespace between
tokens, non-ASCII characters literal (never `\uXXXX` escaped).

1. **Layered resolution, unordered tiers, deletions, unicode and odd keys.**
   Run `python3 settings_engine.py resolve --slug acme-alice`. Exit code 0, stderr may be
   anything, and stdout must be exactly one line equal to the canonical JSON of:
   ```json
   {"applied_layers": ["base.global", "user.alice", "group.engineering"],
    "deleted_paths": [["flags"], ["keep"], ["limits", "nested", "deep", "b"]],
    "document": {"": "empty-key-global", "1": "one", "10": "ten", "2": "two",
                 "__type__": "global-type", "emoji🙂": "group",
                 "extra": {"x": {"y": {"z": true}}}, "features": ["c"], "id": 5,
                 "limits": {"cpu": 8, "mem": 1024, "nested": {"deep": {"a": 1, "c": 3}}},
                 "theme": "dark", "日本語": "group"},
    "revision": 3,
    "slug": "acme-alice"}
   ```
   Additionally assert on the raw stdout line that the numeric-string keys appear in the order
   `"1"`, `"10"`, `"2"`, that the literal characters `日本語` and `emoji🙂` are present, that
   `\u` never appears, that there is no `, ` or `: ` sequence outside string values, and that the
   line count is 1.
2. **Empty objects, object-over-scalar and object-over-array conflicts, absent-key nulls.**
   Run `resolve --slug acme-bob`. Exit 0 and stdout equal to the canonical JSON of:
   ```json
   {"applied_layers": ["base.global", "user.bob"],
    "deleted_paths": [[""], ["1"]],
    "document": {"10": "ten", "2": "two", "__type__": "global-type", "features": {},
                 "flags": {"beta": {}, "gamma": true}, "id": "global-id", "keep": "global",
                 "limits": {"cpu": 2, "mem": 512, "nested": {"deep": {"a": 1, "b": 2}}},
                 "theme": {"nested": true}},
    "revision": 3,
    "slug": "acme-bob"}
   ```
3. **Empty result document and skipped inactive layer.** `resolve --slug solo-empty` must exit 0
   and print the canonical JSON of `{"applied_layers": ["base.empty"], "deleted_paths": [],
   "document": {}, "revision": 0, "slug": "solo-empty"}`.
4. **Records with no applicable layers.** `resolve --slug ghost-town` and
   `resolve --slug orphan-record` must both exit 0 and print an envelope with
   `applied_layers` `[]`, `deleted_paths` `[]`, `document` `{}` and `revision` `0`, with the
   matching `slug`.
5. **Bulk seeded records.** For `fill-0000`, `fill-0157` and `fill-0299`, `resolve --slug
   fill-<n>` must exit 0 and print the canonical JSON of `{"applied_layers": ["fill-<n>.g",
   "fill-<n>.u"], "deleted_paths": [], "document": {"g": {"i": <i>, "x": true},
   "u": {"i": <i>}}, "revision": 0, "slug": "fill-<n>"}`.
6. **Live data, not baked-in answers.** `resolve --slug zz-dynamic` (the record created during
   setup, after the agent finished) must exit 0 and print the canonical JSON of
   `{"applied_layers": ["dyn.mid", "dyn.base"], "deleted_paths": [], "document":
   {"arr": [1, 2, 3], "only": "mid", "p": {"q": 1, "r": 2}}, "revision": 11,
   "slug": "zz-dynamic"}`. Then flip `dyn.off` to active, set its `precedence` on `zz-dynamic` to
   `7` (already the case), set `dyn.base`'s `doc` to `{"p": null, "arr": []}` by a direct
   database write, and immediately re-run the same command: it must now exit 0 and print the
   canonical JSON of `{"applied_layers": ["dyn.mid", "dyn.off", "dyn.base"],
   "deleted_paths": [["p"]], "document": {"arr": [], "nope": 1, "only": "mid"},
   "revision": 111, "slug": "zz-dynamic"}`. Finally activate `dyn.top` by a direct database
   write and re-run the command once more: it must exit 0 and print the canonical JSON of
   `{"applied_layers": ["dyn.mid", "dyn.off", "dyn.base", "dyn.top"], "deleted_paths": [["p"]],
   "document": {"arr": [], "nope": 1, "only": "mid", "p": {"q": 42}}, "revision": 112,
   "slug": "zz-dynamic"}` — the removal stays reported even though a later layer re-created the
   key.
7. **Idempotent read path.** Run `resolve --slug acme-alice` twice more and require byte-identical
   stdout, then verify with a direct database read that `base.global.revision` is still 3,
   `user.alice.revision` is still 0 and `base.global.doc` is unchanged.
8. **Patch: recursive merge, stored nulls, isolation.** Restore the mutable fixtures to their
   baseline (setup step 3) first. Write `/home/user/settings-engine/p1.json` containing
   `{"a": {"c": null, "d": {"e": [9]}}, "new": {"deep": {"x": 1}}, "z": null}` and run
   `patch --slug patch-target --layer patch.user --file p1.json`. Exit 0 and stdout equal to the
   canonical JSON of:
   ```json
   {"applied_layers": ["patch.base", "patch.user"],
    "deleted_paths": [["a", "c"], ["z"]],
    "document": {"a": {"b": 2, "d": {"e": [9]}}, "new": {"deep": {"x": 1}}},
    "revision": 1,
    "slug": "patch-target"}
   ```
   Then verify by direct database read that `patch.user.doc` is exactly
   `{"a": {"b": 2, "c": null, "d": {"e": [9]}}, "new": {"deep": {"x": 1}}, "z": null}`,
   `patch.user.revision` is 1, `patch.base.doc` is still `{"a": {"b": 1, "c": [1, 2]},
   "z": "zed"}` with revision 0, and `patch.shadow` is untouched.
9. **Patch idempotency.** Restore the baseline again, then run the step-8 command twice in a row.
   Both invocations exit 0; the first reports `revision` 1 and the second is identical to the
   step-8 output except that `revision` is 2. `patch.user.doc` in the database must be identical
   after the first and after the second run, and `patch.user.revision` must be 2.
10. **Patching an inactive layer.** Restore the baseline, write
    `/home/user/settings-engine/p2.json` containing `{"shadow2": {"k": false}}` and run
    `patch --slug patch-target --layer patch.shadow --file p2.json`. Exit 0, and the printed
    envelope must be the canonical JSON of `{"applied_layers": ["patch.base", "patch.user"],
    "deleted_paths": [], "document": {"a": {"b": 2, "c": [1, 2]}, "z": "zed"}, "revision": 0,
    "slug": "patch-target"}`. A direct database read must show `patch.shadow.doc` equal to
    `{"shadow": true, "shadow2": {"k": false}}`, `patch.shadow.revision` equal to 1,
    `patch.shadow` still inactive, and `patch.user` untouched (`{"a": {"b": 2}}`, revision 0).
11. **Unknown record.** `resolve --slug nope-nope` must exit 3 with empty stdout and non-empty
    stderr. `patch --slug nope-nope --layer patch.user --file p1.json` must also exit 3.
12. **Error precedence.** `patch --slug nope-nope --layer no.such.layer --file
    /home/user/settings-engine/does-not-exist.json` must exit 3 (record error wins).
13. **Layer not in the chain.** After restoring the baseline,
    `patch --slug patch-target --layer base.global --file p1.json`
    must exit 4 with empty stdout and non-empty stderr, even though `base.global` exists;
    `patch --slug patch-target --layer no.such.layer --file p1.json` must exit 4 as well. After
    both, `base.global` must be unchanged (revision 3, seeded `doc`) and `patch.user` must still
    be `{"a": {"b": 2}}` at revision 0.
14. **Invalid patch documents.** After restoring the baseline, with
    `/home/user/settings-engine/bad1.json` containing
    `{"a": ` (truncated), `/home/user/settings-engine/bad2.json` containing `[1, 2, 3]`, and
    `/home/user/settings-engine/bad3.json` containing `"just a string"`, each of
    `patch --slug patch-target --layer patch.user --file bad1.json`, `... bad2.json`,
    `... bad3.json` and `patch --slug patch-target --layer patch.user --file
    /home/user/settings-engine/does-not-exist.json` must exit 5 with empty stdout and non-empty
    stderr, and afterwards `patch.user` must still be `{"a": {"b": 2}}` at revision 0.
15. **Concurrent patches.** Restore `race.base` (`{"seed": "kept", "counterparts": {"pre": 1}}`,
    revision 0) and `race.user` (`{}`, revision 0) to their baseline first.
    Write eight files `/home/user/settings-engine/race_<i>.json` for `i`
    in 0..7, file `i` containing `{"k<i>": {"n": <i>}, "shared": {"s<i>": <i>}}`. Start all eight
    `patch --slug race-target --layer race.user --file race_<i>.json` commands simultaneously and
    wait for all of them. Every one must exit 0. Then a direct database read must show
    `race.user.revision` equal to 8 and `race.user.doc` equal to `{"k0": {"n": 0}, ...,
    "k7": {"n": 7}, "shared": {"s0": 0, "s1": 1, ..., "s7": 7}}` — all eight keys and all eight
    nested `shared` sub-keys present. `race.base` must be untouched.
    Finally `resolve --slug race-target` must exit 0 and print `document` equal to
    `{"counterparts": {"pre": 1}, "k0": {"n": 0}, ..., "k7": {"n": 7}, "seed": "kept",
    "shared": {"s0": 0, ..., "s7": 7}}` with `revision` 8.
16. **Regression: seeded data otherwise intact.** By direct database read, assert there are
    exactly 307 `SettingsRecord` objects whose `slug` does not start with `zz-` and exactly 914
    `SettingsLayer` objects whose `key` does not start with `dyn.`; that `acme-alice`'s `label`
    is `Acme / Alice` and its chain is exactly the four seeded layer keys; that
    `group.engineering.doc`, `user.alice.doc`, `user.bob.doc`, `base.empty.doc` and
    `race.base.doc` are byte-equivalent to the seeded values above with their seeded `revision`
    values; that `override.disabled.revision` is still 41 and it is still inactive; that
    every `fill-*` layer still has `revision` 0; and that every `fill-*.x` layer is still
    inactive.
17. **CLI sanity through the Gel CLI itself.** With the server ready, `gel query 'select 1'`
    (run from the project directory) must exit 0, and `gel migration status` must exit 0,
    proving the seeded migration state was not broken.
